newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slumps to weak close, breaches $21.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slumps to weak close, breaches $21.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were slapped down by around a further 60 cents in a wave of late concerted selling on the back of a NYMEX slump, brokers said.
The prompt March contract broke through the $21 a barrel barrier just ahead of the close to reach a low of $20.89, the bottom of a trading range of almost a dollar.
It closed at $21.02, 67 cents down on the session, with impressive trading volume building up over day.
The move was seen technically driven after Thursday's significant falls with contracts across the complex tumbling over themselves in the downward dive.
"There was not real leader although the crudes were weakest," one broker said. "Every support was broken and there was just noting to stop it going further on down."

The move swept steadily through a chart gap left from late August which took the contract down to the $21.00 level. That was heralded when March took out the $21.45 top of the gap, starting its steady decline on the back of falling NTMEX crude, brokers said.
The move completed a week in which Brent has dropped around $1.50, loosing its fundamental support from distillates and with the physical market also waning.
Earlier, gas oil futures stages a modest come-back, but still closed lower, deepening Thursday's losses.
February last trade $1.50 down at $190.25 a tonne, up from a session low of $186.00.
Poor physical demand was also seen underlying the technical weakness of that market.
